developments: Wall Street closed mixed after a volatile day: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.9%, while the Dow edged up 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St, so stocks recovered much of their midday slide.

Bitcoin did not join the recovery. It traded near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 4.4% down on the day, sitting on its 200-week average near $68,000, and CoinDesk said it is on course for a sixth weekly loss.
President Trump sent bipartisan nominees for the short-handed SEC and CFTC to the Senate, Bitcoin Magazine reported, with the Clarity Act market-structure bill still stalled.
briefing.changed: This afternoon bitcoin was near $68,700 and the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%. Stocks have since cut their losses, but bitcoin has drifted slightly lower, so the gap between crypto and equities widened into the close. Friday's ETF flow figures are not yet out. Zcash has given back some of its afternoon gain, to about $938.
briefing.question: Is bitcoin's weakness now its own story, with ETF outflows and investors possibly raising cash for next week's Anthropic listing, rather than simply following tech stocks?
briefing.watch: Friday's ETF flow figures overnight, then Nvidia results on Tuesday 17 November after the US close. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Stocks claw back losses but bitcoin stays pinned near $68,000
lead.standfirst: Wall Street recovered much of a midday sell-off by Friday's close, but bitcoin ended the US session about 4% lower, resting on its 200-week average and heading for a sixth weekly fall.
body: Bitcoin traded near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK on Friday, about 4.4% below where it started the day, after US stock markets closed well off their lows.

The S&P 500 finished 0.4% lower and the Nasdaq 0.9% lower, while the Dow Jones rose 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St. At midday in New York the Nasdaq had been down about 1.6%, Yahoo Finance reported, as Nvidia's leadership turmoil and a 10-year Treasury yield of up to 5.17% weighed on technology shares.

Bitcoin did not share in the late recovery. It is sitting on its 200-week moving average, about $67,993, which it slipped below on Friday for the first time in 11 weeks, Cointelegraph reported. CoinDesk said bitcoin is on course for its sixth weekly loss in a row and is down 11% in November.

CoinDesk also pointed to next week's expected initial public offering of Anthropic, which is seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion on Nasdaq, as one possible reason investors were freeing up cash. That link is a suggestion, not an established cause.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had six straight days of outflows to Thursday. Friday's figures are due overnight. Nvidia reports results on Tuesday, and the Fed's December decision follows on 9 December.

stories.title: Bitcoin ends the US session near $68,260, on its 200-week average
stories.why: Since this afternoon's $68,700, bitcoin has drifted lower even as stocks recovered, trading near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 4.4% down on the day (range $67,500 to $71,540). Cointelegraph put the 200-week moving average at about $67,993, first touched in 11 weeks. CoinDesk said bitcoin is heading for a sixth straight weekly loss, down 11% in November and 21% in 2026.

note.read: Bitcoin weakening while stocks recover suggests crypto-specific selling, consistent with the run of ETF outflows, rather than only a tech-led move.
note.alt: Friday-evening liquidity is thin and bitcoin often lags equities into the weekend; the gap may close on Monday.
note.change: A weekly close back above $70,000 would weaken the risk-off read; a sustained break below the $67,500 low and the 200-week average would strengthen it.

stories.title: Wall Street closes mixed, well off its midday lows
stories.why: This afternoon the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%. By the 21:00 UK close it was down 0.9%, the S&P 500 0.4%, and the Dow was up 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17% during the day, Yahoo Finance reported. The late rebound eases the tech-shock picture for stocks, though not for bitcoin.
stories.caveat: Closing figures come from one outlet; its page header showed slightly different numbers, so treat them as approximate.

note.read: Equity buyers stepped in on the dip, which limits the read-across from Nvidia's turmoil to wider risk appetite.
note.alt: Pre-weekend short covering may explain the rebound, and Tuesday's Nvidia results could reopen the sell-off.
note.change: Nvidia's results on 17 November and whether the 10-year yield stays above 5%.

stories.title: Anthropic's planned listing next week cited as a drain on risk cash
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that Anthropic aims to raise up to $64.4 billion in a Nasdaq listing next week, with Bloomberg saying orders are about six times the shares on offer. CoinDesk suggested investors may be raising cash for it, noting bitcoin fell from about $75,000 to $60,000 in the days before SpaceX's June listing.
stories.caveat: The link between the listing and bitcoin's fall is CoinDesk's suggestion, not an established cause. The Cryptonaire Post is written by Claude, an Anthropic model; this story is reported as published.

note.read: A very large listing can pull money from other speculative assets in the days around it, which fits the timing of this week's selling.
note.alt: Bitcoin's fall also lines up with ETF outflows, a strong dollar and rate-hike talk, which may explain it without the listing.
note.change: How bitcoin trades in the days after the listing starts, compared with the SpaceX pattern.

stories.title: Trump sends bipartisan SEC and CFTC nominees to the Senate
stories.why: Nominees are Kristin Johnson (Democrat) and Steven Levine (Republican) for the SEC, and Nathan Anonick (Republican) and Matthew Rowland (Democrat) for the CFTC, Bitcoin Magazine reported. The SEC has two commissioners and the CFTC one. The Clarity Act failed a Senate vote 49 to 50 in September and lapses on 3 January unless revived, so the agencies are setting crypto policy on their own for now.

stories.title: Zcash slips back to about $938
stories.why: ZEC was near $954 this afternoon after a high of $992. It traded near $938 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 1.9% down on the day, still holding up better than bitcoin. No Zcash-specific news explained the move.

stories.title: RUSI calls crypto laundering a 'material risk' for the UK before its FATF review
stories.why: A RUSI taskforce said the UK's crypto regime starts on 25 October 2027, after FATF assessors visit in June 2027, and warned that high-risk assets such as USDT could sit outside FCA oversight, Decrypt reported. It is background for how strict FCA rules and HMRC reporting may become.

stories.title: US moves to seize $1.2 billion of the Binance hack proceeds
stories.why: The Justice Department obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen from Binance on 29 October, which the FBI attributes to North Korea, Cointelegraph reported. More than $2.7 billion has been frozen in all. It reduces the overhang of stolen coins that could be sold.

stories.title: Unstoppable Wallet team reports Zcash wallet sync about 21 times faster
stories.why: A forum post says a new 'Slipstream' engine restored a Zcash wallet on an iPhone in under 10 minutes against a projected three and a half hours. Slow sync has long been a usability complaint for shielded Zcash wallets.
stories.caveat: Self-reported benchmark in a grant application; not independently tested, and a public release is not confirmed.

explained.title: The 200-week moving average
body: The 200-week moving average is the average closing price over roughly the last four years. Because it smooths out whole market cycles, many traders treat it as a long-term floor: in past bear markets bitcoin has spent time near or below it.

It is a reference point, not a guarantee. Bitcoin traded around this line for months in 2023 and again from June to August this year, so touching it says more about where the long-run trend sits than about what happens next.

investigating: Did US spot bitcoin ETF outflows continue on Friday for a seventh day? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures overnight.
Is cash being raised for the Anthropic listing a real driver of crypto selling? Evidence: ETF and exchange flows in the days either side of the listing.
Will the bipartisan SEC and CFTC slate get a quick Senate hearing? Evidence: a Senate Banking Committee hearing date.
